content: Metaproterenol is a medication prescribed to manage and alleviate wheezing, shortness of breath, and difficulty breathing associated with conditions such as asthma, chronic bronchitis, emphysema, and other pulmonary diseases. It works by relaxing and dilating the airways in the lungs, facilitating easier breathing. While it is primarily used for these purposes, it may also be prescribed for other conditions. Consult your physician or pharmacist for additional information. Metaproterenol is available in various forms, including tablets, syrup, an inhalation solution, and an aerosol inhaler. The medication is typically administered via oral inhalation as needed to relieve symptoms or every 3-4 hours to prevent them. Alternatively, it may be taken orally three to four times daily. It is crucial to follow the instructions on your prescription label meticulously and seek clarification from your doctor or pharmacist if needed. Use metaproterenol exactly as prescribed, avoiding any deviation in dosage or frequency. If using the inhaler for asthma attacks, do not exceed 12 puffs in a single day. While metaproterenol helps control symptoms of asthma and other lung conditions, it does not cure them. Continue using the medication even if you feel well, and do not discontinue it without consulting your doctor. Before using the metaproterenol inhaler for the first time, carefully read the accompanying written instructions. Request a demonstration of the correct technique from your doctor, pharmacist, or respiratory therapist, and practice under their supervision. To use the inhaler properly, follow these steps: 1. Shake the inhaler thoroughly. 2. Remove the protective cap. 3. Exhale completely through your nose while keeping your mouth closed. 4. For the open-mouth technique, open your mouth wide and position the mouthpiece 1-2 inches away from your mouth. For the closed-mouth technique, place the mouthpiece well into your mouth, past your front teeth, and seal your lips tightly around it. 5. Inhale slowly and deeply through the mouthpiece while simultaneously pressing down on the container to release the medication. 6. Hold your breath for 5-10 seconds, then remove the inhaler and exhale slowly through your nose or mouth. 7. If a second puff is required, wait 2 minutes, shake the inhaler again, and repeat the process. 8. Replace the protective cap on the inhaler after use. If you experience difficulty delivering the medication into your lungs, a spacer device may be helpful. Consult your doctor, pharmacist, or respiratory therapist for guidance. Before starting metaproterenol, inform your doctor and pharmacist if you are allergic to this medication or any other drugs. Provide a complete list of all prescription and nonprescription medications, vitamins, and supplements you are taking, especially atenolol, carteolol, labetalol, metoprolol, nadolol, phenelzine, propranolol, sotalol, theophylline, timolol, tranylcypromine, or medications for asthma, heart disease, or depression. Be cautious with over-the-counter products containing ephedrine, phenylephrine, phenylpropanolamine, or pseudoephedrine, as these are commonly found in diet pills and cold or asthma medications. Always consult your doctor before taking these products, even if you have used them without issues in the past. Additionally, notify your doctor if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding. If you become pregnant while taking metaproterenol, contact your doctor immediately. If you are scheduled for surgery, including dental procedures, inform your surgeon or dentist that you are taking this medication. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is nearly time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and resume your regular schedule. Do not take a double dose to compensate for a missed one. Metaproterenol may cause side effects. Notify your doctor if you experience any of the following symptoms, especially if they are severe or persistent: tremor, nervousness, dizziness, weakness, headache, upset stomach, cough, dry mouth, or throat irritation. Serious side effects requiring immediate medical attention include increased difficulty breathing, rapid or irregular heartbeat, or chest pain. Report any severe side effects to your doctor or the FDA’s MedWatch program. Store metaproterenol in its original container, tightly sealed, and out of reach of children. Keep it at room temperature, away from excessive heat and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Discard the solution if it appears pink, yellow, or darker than usual, or if it contains floating particles. Dispose of expired or unused medication properly, consulting your pharmacist for guidance. Avoid puncturing the container and do not discard it in a fire or incinerator. In case of overdose, contact your local poison control center at 1-800-222-1222. If the individual collapses or stops breathing, call emergency services at 911. Attend all scheduled appointments with your doctor and laboratory, as certain tests may be required to monitor your response to metaproterenol. To alleviate dry mouth or throat irritation caused by inhalation, rinse your mouth with water, chew gum, or suck on sugarless hard candy after use. Clean inhalation devices weekly by removing the drug container from the plastic mouthpiece, washing the mouthpiece with warm water, and drying it thoroughly. Do not share your medication with others. If you have questions about refilling your prescription, consult your pharmacist. Metaproterenol is marketed under the brand names Alupent®, Alupent® Inhalation Solution, and Alupent® Syrup.
